mainTopic: The גיד הנשה of a non-kosher animal and of a נבלה, and when one prohibition can take hold on another (איסור כולל, איסור חמור), proven from a טמא who eats impure קדשים.
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא: רבי שמעון exempts someone who eats the גיד הנשה of a non-kosher animal. The גמרא challenges this with a מה נפשך argument. רבא answers that sinews have no meat-taste, and a פסוק limits the גיד prohibition to animals whose meat is permitted. Next, רב יהודה quotes רב about the גיד of a נבלה: רבי מאיר says the eater is liable twice, and the חכמים say only once. The חכמים agree, though, that the גיד of an עולה or a שור הנסקל brings two punishments. רבא says this split view belongs to רבי יוסי הגלילי, and he proves it from a משנה about a טמא who eats impure קדשים. He explains that they argue only when the meat became impure first: the חכמים use איסור כולל (מגו), and רבי יוסי הגלילי rejects it. Finally the גמרא asks why the stricter טומאת הגוף does not take hold anyway. רב אשי answers that טומאת בשר may be the stricter one, since impure meat can never be purified in a מקוה.

steps.title: רבי שמעון exempts the eater of a non-kosher animal's sciatic nerve
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of the ברייתא: רבי שמעון holds that one who eats the גיד הנשה of a non-kosher animal is completely exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the last part of a ברייתא: about someone who eats the גיד הנשה of a non-kosher animal, רבי שמעון says he gets no punishment at all. This sets up the question the גמרא is about to ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון does not just reduce the punishment, he removes it completely. That is surprising, because the person ate something that seems forbidden in two ways: it comes from a non-kosher animal, and it is a גיד הנשה.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempts; says the person is not liable for punishment
The sciatic nerve, which the Torah forbids eating
A non-kosher animal

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon exempts him.
phrases.notes: This wraps up a ברייתא about eating the גיד הנשה of a non-kosher animal; just before this, רבי יהודה made him liable twice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun before this section, giving רבי שמעון's opposing view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, one who eats the גיד הנשה of a non-kosher animal is completely exempt.

steps.title: Whichever way you look at it, רבי שמעון should make him liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון: whether or not one prohibition can take hold on another, and even if sinews have no meat-taste, he should still be liable for something.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי שמעון, whichever way you look at it there is a problem. If one prohibition can take hold where another already exists, he should also be liable for the גיד. If one prohibition cannot take hold on another, he should be liable for the non-kosher prohibition, which came first. And if sinews do not have the taste of meat, so the non-kosher prohibition does not apply, he should be liable for the גיד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי שמעון can exempt the person completely. It goes through every possible reason and shows that each one still leaves some prohibition in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three options. If איסור חל על איסור, both prohibitions apply. If not, the earlier one (the non-kosher prohibition) should apply. If the non-kosher prohibition does not apply because a sinew is not real meat, then nothing blocks the גיד prohibition. In no case does the person go completely free.

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you want it; an argument that every option leads to a problem
A second prohibition takes hold on something already forbidden
Let him be liable; he should be liable
Which came first
Gives taste; here, whether sinews count as having the taste of meat

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word טומאה does not mean ritual impurity. It means the prohibition of eating a non-kosher (טמאה) animal.

phrases.english: But Rabbi Shimon, whichever way you look at it?
If a prohibition takes hold on a prohibition,
let him be liable also because of the sciatic nerve;

phrases.aramaic: אִי אֵין אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר –
phrases.english: if a prohibition does not take hold on a prohibition,
let him be liable because of non-kosher status, which came first;
and if sinews do not have the quality of giving taste,
phrases.notes: He means that if a sinew does not count as meat, it would not fall under the non-kosher meat prohibition.

phrases.english: let him be liable because of the sciatic nerve.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of רבי שמעון just stated.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's total exemption for eating the גיד הנשה of a non-kosher animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every possible view (איסור חל על איסור, אין איסור חל על איסור, אין בגידים בנותן טעם) leaves at least one prohibition in force, so a full exemption seems impossible.

steps.title: רבא: sinews have no meat-taste, and the verse limits the sciatic nerve to permitted animals
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי שמעון holds sinews have no meat-taste, so the non-kosher prohibition does not apply, and a פסוק teaches that the גיד prohibition only applies to an animal whose meat is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Really, he holds that sinews have no meat-taste. But that case is different, because the פסוק says: 'Therefore the children of Israel do not eat the sciatic nerve.' This means an animal whose גיד is forbidden and whose meat is permitted. That leaves out this animal, whose גיד is forbidden and whose meat is also forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by picking the third option: sinews have no meat-taste. He then explains why the גיד prohibition still does not apply: the פסוק only speaks about animals whose meat is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that if the non-kosher prohibition is removed, the גיד prohibition takes over. רבא says no: the גיד prohibition never applied to non-kosher animals in the first place, because the Torah only forbids the גיד of an animal whose meat is permitted. So neither prohibition applies, and רבי שמעון's full exemption makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Really; actually (keeping the original assumption)
It is different there
A פסוק; a verse
This one is excluded

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, the גיד הנשה prohibition only applies to animals whose meat is permitted, so a non-kosher animal's גיד carries no punishment at all.

phrases.english: Rava said: Actually he holds
that sinews do not have the quality of giving taste,
and it is different there, because the verse says:
phrases.notes: "There" is the גיד prohibition, which gets its own limit from the פסוק.

phrases.english: "Therefore the children of Israel do not eat
the sciatic nerve":
one whose nerve is forbidden and whose meat is permitted;

phrases.aramaic: יָצְתָה זוֹ שֶׁגִּידוֹ אָסוּר וּבְשָׂרוֹ אָסוּר.
phrases.english: this is excluded, whose nerve is forbidden and whose meat is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לְעוֹלָם קָסָבַר אֵין בְּגִידִים בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מה נפשך challenge by accepting its third option and closing the gap it pointed out.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts one side of the dilemma and adds a limit from a פסוק that blocks the expected liability.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If sinews have no meat-taste, the non-kosher prohibition is gone, so the גיד prohibition should apply.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גיד prohibition never applies to non-kosher animals, because the פסוק limits it to animals whose meat is permitted, so neither prohibition applies.

steps.title: Eating the sciatic nerve of a נבלה: two liabilities or one
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: for one who eats the גיד הנשה of a נבלה, רבי מאיר says he is liable twice, and the חכמים say only once.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: One who eats the גיד הנשה of a נבלה: רבי מאיר makes him liable twice, and the חכמים say he is liable only once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: the גיד of a kosher animal that died without proper שחיטה. It records a מחלוקת about how many punishments the eater receives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike a non-kosher animal, a נבלה comes from a kosher species, so the limit רבא just gave from the פסוק does not apply. The question now is whether the person is punished for both the גיד and the נבלה prohibition, or only once.

keyTerms.meaning: A kosher animal that died without proper שחיטה
Makes him liable twice; two sets of punishment
He is liable only once

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said, Rav said:
One who eats the sciatic nerve of an unslaughtered carcass:
Rabbi Meir makes him liable for two,

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא אַחַת.
phrases.english: and the Rabbis say: He is liable for only one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר רַב: הָאוֹכֵל גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה שֶׁל נְבֵלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the גיד of a non-kosher animal to the גיד of a kosher animal that became a נבלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For eating the גיד הנשה of a נבלה, רבי מאיר says he is liable twice, and the חכמים say only once.

steps.title: The חכמים agree: an עולה or a שור הנסקל brings two punishments
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים concede that someone who eats the גיד הנשה of an עולה or of a שור הנסקל is liable twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים agree with רבי מאיר that someone who eats the גיד הנשה of an עולה, or of a שור הנסקל, is liable twice.
steps.whatsHappening: The statement quoted by רב continues. The חכמים, who said 'only once' about a נבלה, agree that in two other cases the eater is liable twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a נבלה, the חכמים said the second prohibition does not take hold on the גיד, which was already forbidden. Here they agree that it does take hold. Being an עולה or a שור הנסקל is a more severe prohibition than נבלה: you may not even get any benefit from these animals, not just eat them.

keyTerms.meaning: They agree. One side admits the other side is right in a specific case.
A burnt offering, which belongs completely to the בית המקדש.
An ox sentenced to be stoned for killing a person. It is forbidden to eat it or to benefit from it.
Liable twice, meaning two sets of lashes.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis agree with Rabbi Meir
regarding one who eats the sciatic nerve
of a burnt offering or of an ox that is stoned,
phrases.notes: In both cases the גיד was already forbidden before the animal became an offering or was sentenced.

phrases.english: that he is liable twice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the statement רב יהודה quoted from רב, adding a case where the חכמים agree with רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For the גיד הנשה of an עולה or a שור הנסקל, even the חכמים hold the eater is liable twice.

steps.title: Which תנא holds this two-part rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who holds that an איסור כולל alone cannot take hold on an existing prohibition, but one that is also an איסור חמור can.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is this תנא? On one hand, he holds that a broader prohibition cannot take hold where there is already a prohibition. On the other hand, he holds that a prohibition that is both broader and more severe can take hold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the rule behind the חכמים's two rulings and asks which known תנא holds it. This sets up רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נבלה forbids the whole animal, so it is broader (כולל) than the גיד, yet the חכמים say it does not take hold on the גיד. An עולה or a שור הנסקל is both broader and more severe (forbidden for benefit), and that does take hold. The גמרא wants a known תנא who holds this exact split.

keyTerms.meaning: A broader prohibition. It covers things that were not forbidden before, together with the thing that already was.
One prohibition taking hold on top of an existing prohibition.
A more severe prohibition, such as one that also forbids any benefit.
Who is this תנא? A question asking which sage holds a certain view.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. For the חכמים, being 'broader' alone (נבלה) is not enough to take hold on the גיד. It takes hold only when the new prohibition is broader and more severe (עולה, שור הנסקל).

phrases.english: And who is this tanna,
who, regarding a broader prohibition,

phrases.aramaic: אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר לֵית לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: does not hold that a prohibition takes hold on a prohibition,
phrases.notes: This is the נבלה case: it does not take hold on the גיד.

phrases.english: but where a broader prohibition is also a more severe prohibition,
phrases.notes: This is the עולה and שור הנסקל case.

phrases.english: he does hold it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which known תנא stands behind the view of the חכמים in steps 4 and 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of a תנא who holds that an איסור כולל alone does not take hold, but an איסור כולל that is also an איסור חמור does.

steps.title: רבא: it is רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: רבא identifies the תנא as רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question: the view of the חכמים matches רבי יוסי הגלילי. Next he brings a source to show it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא connects an anonymous view to a named sage. The proof in the next step shows that רבי יוסי הגלילי holds an איסור כולל cannot take hold on an existing prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: It is. Used when the גמרא names the author of a view.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי הִיא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא is רבי יוסי הגלילי.

steps.title: Proof from a משנה about an impure person eating קדשים
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a משנה. The first view says an impure person who eats any קדשים is liable. רבי יוסי הגלילי says that if the קדשים were already impure, he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: an impure person who ate holy food is liable, whether the food was impure or pure. רבי יוסי הגלילי says: an impure person who ate pure holy food is liable, but an impure person who ate impure holy food is exempt, because he only ate something impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a משנה to prove that רבי יוסי הגלילי holds an איסור כולל does not take hold on an existing prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Impure holy meat is already forbidden to eat. When the person becomes impure, a new prohibition starts, and it is broader because it now forbids him even pure holy food. רבי יוסי הגלילי says he is exempt for the impure meat, so this broader prohibition did not take hold on meat that was already forbidden. That matches the חכמים's view about נבלה and the גיד.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritually impure. Here it describes both the person and the food.
Ritually pure.
Holy food, such as the meat of offerings.
Exempt, meaning not liable to punishment.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that a prohibition which is only broader (כולל) does not take hold on something already forbidden. רבא says this is the view of the חכמים, who said 'only once' for the גיד הנשה of a נבלה.

phrases.english: As we learned: an impure person who ate holy food,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in זבחים 106a.

phrases.english: whether it was impure holy food
or pure holy food, is liable.
Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
An impure person who ate pure holy food is liable,
but an impure person who ate impure holy food is exempt,
since he only ate an impure thing.
phrases.notes: He means the food was already forbidden for being impure, so the person's own impurity adds nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind רבא's answer in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי הגלילי holds an איסור כולל does not take hold on an existing prohibition.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in זבחים: an impure person who eats impure holy food is exempt according to רבי יוסי הגלילי.

steps.title: The חכמים push back: a טמא who eats pure meat also makes it impure
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer רבי יוסי הגלילי: even when a טמא eats pure קדשים, he makes them impure by touching them first, and he is still liable. So he should be liable for impure קדשים too.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Even an impure person who eats pure sacrificial meat makes it impure as soon as he touches it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is still part of the quoted משנה. The חכמים attack רבי יוסי הגלילי's ruling with a case everyone agrees on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי said that once the meat is already impure, the טמא is exempt. The חכמים point out that a טמא eating pure meat always makes it impure by touching it before he eats it, so by that logic he would never be liable. Since he certainly is liable, the meat already being impure should not exempt him either.

keyTerms.meaning: An impure person, here one who is forbidden to eat קדשים
Pure; here, sacrificial meat that has not become impure
Touched
He made it impure

phrases.english: They said to him:
phrases.notes: "They" are the חכמים, answering רבי יוסי הגלילי from step 8.

phrases.english: Even an impure person who ate pure [sacrificial meat],
once he touched it, he made it impure.
phrases.notes: The rest is left unsaid: yet he is surely liable, so he should be liable for impure meat too.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אַף טָמֵא שֶׁאָכַל אֶת הַטָּהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The חכמים in the quoted משנה rebut רבי יוסי הגלילי's ruling from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי הגלילי's ruling that a טמא who eats already-impure קדשים is exempt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A טמא always makes pure meat impure by touching it before eating, and he is still liable. So the meat already being impure cannot be a reason to exempt him.

steps.title: The חכמים' argument looks convincing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא remarks that the חכמים are arguing well. So how can רבי יוסי הגלילי disagree?
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים are making a good point to רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps outside the משנה and says the חכמים' argument seems unanswerable. This sets up רבא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is left unspoken: if the argument is this strong, what is רבי יוסי הגלילי's position? The גמרא needs to show that his view still makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Well, correctly
They are saying
The Rabbis, meaning the חכמים in the משנה

phrases.english: The Rabbis are saying well to him,
to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.
phrases.notes: The question is implied: so how does רבי יוסי הגלילי answer them?

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁפִּיר קָא אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא sides with the force of the חכמים' argument in step 9 and challenges רבי יוסי הגלילי's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי הגלילי's position in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים' argument from a טמא eating pure meat seems to show that the meat already being impure makes no difference.

steps.title: If the person became impure first, everyone agrees he is liable
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that when the person became impure before the meat did, everyone agrees he is liable, because the כרת prohibition came first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Where the person became impure first and the meat became impure afterward, everyone agrees he is liable, because the prohibition carrying כרת came first.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins to answer for רבי יוסי הגלילי by marking off the cases where there is no argument at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition of a טמא eating קדשים carries כרת. If the person was already impure, that prohibition was in place before the meat became impure, so it clearly applies. This also covers the חכמים' case of a טמא touching pure meat: he was impure first, so רבי יוסי הגלילי agrees he is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Spiritual cutting off, the punishment for a טמא eating קדשים
Came first
Everyone, meaning both sides agree
The body, meaning the person himself

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the order in which the two prohibitions began is what decides the case. That is how רבי יוסי הגלילי escapes the חכמים' argument.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
Where the body became impure
and afterward the meat became impure,
everyone agrees that he is liable,
because the prohibition carrying karet came first.
phrases.notes: This is the prohibition of an impure person eating holy meat, which was already on him before the meat became impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: בְּנִטְמָא הַגּוּף וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִטְמָא בָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 by limiting where the argument applies.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים' case of a טמא eating pure meat seemed to defeat רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.terutzMaskana: In that case the person was impure first, so even רבי יוסי הגלילי agrees he is liable.

steps.title: The real argument: meat impure first, and the חכמים' reasoning
steps.stepSummary: The argument is only where the meat became impure first. The חכמים apply איסור כולל: since he is now forbidden to eat all pure pieces, he is forbidden to eat the impure piece as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue where the meat became impure first and the person afterward. The חכמים hold of איסור כולל: since he is now liable for all the ordinary pure pieces, he is also liable for the impure piece.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא names the case that is actually in dispute and explains why the חכמים say he is liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the prohibition against eating impure meat came first, so the כרת prohibition would normally not be able to take effect on top of it. The חכמים say it does, because when the person became impure, a new prohibition covered every pure piece of קדשים, and because of that it covers this impure piece too.

keyTerms.meaning: An inclusive prohibition: a new prohibition that spreads to more things, so it can take hold even where something was already forbidden
They hold of, they accept
A piece of meat
In general, ordinary ones
He is liable

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about whether he is liable at all. Even רבי יוסי הגלילי forbids him to eat impure meat. The question is only whether the כרת prohibition of a טמא also takes hold on top of the earlier one.

phrases.english: Where they disagree

phrases.aramaic: בְּנִטְמָא בָּשָׂר, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִטְמָא הַגּוּף.
phrases.english: is where the meat became impure, and afterward the body became impure.
The Rabbis hold of an inclusive prohibition,
that since he is liable
for the ordinary pure pieces,
phrases.notes: He means the pure pieces of holy meat, which were permitted to him until he became impure.

phrases.english: he is also liable for the impure piece.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי פְּלִיגִי בְּנִטְמָא בָּשָׂר, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִטְמָא הַגּוּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's answer by naming the disputed case and the חכמים' reasoning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the principle behind the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that the חכמים and רבי יוסי הגלילי disagree about every case of a טמא eating impure meat.
steps.terutzMaskana: They disagree only when the meat became impure first. The חכמים apply איסור כולל to make him liable.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי does not accept the "since" reasoning
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי does not accept איסור כולל, because he does not use the reasoning of מגו (since).
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי הגלילי does not hold of איסור כולל, because we do not say מגו ("since").
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his explanation by giving רבי יוסי הגלילי's reasoning. This closes the answer to the challenge from step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי הגלילי, the fact that the new prohibition covers pure pieces does not carry it over to a piece that was already forbidden. So when the meat became impure first, the כרת prohibition does not take hold, and he is exempt from it. This matches step 7, where רבא named him as the one who says איסור כולל alone is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: "Since": since a rule applies to some cases, it carries over to this case too
He does not hold of
We do not say, meaning we do not use this reasoning

steps.whatToRemember: If the person became impure first, everyone agrees he is liable. If the meat became impure first, the חכמים say he is liable through איסור כולל and מגו, while רבי יוסי הגלילי says he is exempt because he does not accept מגו.
steps.whyThisMatters: This backs up רבא's claim in step 7 that רבי יוסי הגלילי is the one who holds that איסור כולל alone cannot take hold on an existing prohibition.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei HaGelili
does not hold of an inclusive prohibition,
because we do not say "since."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי לֵית לֵיהּ אִיסּוּר כּוֹלֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's explanation with רבי יוסי הגלילי's side of the dispute.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוסי הגלילי rejects מגו, so איסור כולל does not take hold on meat that was already impure. This confirms he is the תנא identified in step 7.

steps.title: Shouldn't the stricter prohibition take effect anyway?
steps.stepSummary: Even if רבי יוסי הגלילי rejects איסור כולל, a stricter prohibition should still take effect on a lighter one. טומאת הגוף carries כרת, so it should apply on top of טומאת בשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי הגלילי: granted, he does not hold of איסור כולל. But when there is already a lenient prohibition, a stringent prohibition should come and take effect on top of it. And what is the stringent one? טומאת הגוף, since eating קדשים with טומאת הגוף is punished with כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי הגלילי from a different angle. It says that even without איסור כולל, there is another rule that should make the person liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said רבי יוסי הגלילי rejects איסור כולל. The גמרא now raises a separate rule: a stricter prohibition can take effect on top of an existing lighter one. Since טומאת הגוף carries כרת, it seems stricter than טומאת בשר, so it should apply even though the meat became impure first.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / even if we accept that
A lighter (more lenient) prohibition
A stricter (more severe) prohibition
It will take effect / apply
The person's own bodily impurity
Spiritual 'cutting off', a very severe punishment

steps.confusionAlert: This is a NEW rule, not איסור כולל again. איסור כולל is about a prohibition that covers more things. Here the argument is only that one prohibition is more severe than the other.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei HaGelili:
granted that he does not accept an inclusive prohibition,
where there is a lenient prohibition, let a stringent prohibition come
and take effect on the lenient prohibition.
And what is it? The impurity of the body,
for impurity of the body is punishable by karet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts step 13 (no איסור כולל) but raises a different rule, איסור חמור, against רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי הגלילי's ruling of no liability when the meat became impure first
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A stricter prohibition takes effect on a lighter one. טומאת הגוף (כרת) seems stricter than טומאת בשר, so it should apply.

steps.title: Maybe the meat's impurity is the stricter one
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that we cannot assume טומאת הגוף is stricter. טומאת בשר may be stricter, because impure meat can never be purified in a מקוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Who tells us that טומאת הגוף is stricter? Maybe טומאת בשר is stricter, since impure meat has no way to become pure in a מקוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends רבי יוסי הגלילי. He questions whether the person's impurity really is the stricter prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in step 14 depended on the claim that טומאת הגוף is stricter. רב אשי points out another side: a person can immerse in a מקוה and become pure, but impure meat stays impure forever. Since it is unclear which one is stricter, we cannot say the person's prohibition takes effect on top of the meat's.

keyTerms.meaning: Who says? (we cannot assume it)
Perhaps
The impurity of the meat itself
Becoming pure by immersing in a ritual bath

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוסי הגלילי, when the meat became impure first, the person is not liable for the כרת prohibition of a טמא eating קדשים. He rejects איסור כולל, and according to רב אשי, איסור חמור doesn't help either, because each impurity is more severe in its own way.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that 'stricter' can be measured in more than one way: by the punishment (כרת) or by how permanent the status is.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Who will tell us
that impurity of the body is more stringent?
Perhaps impurity of the meat is more stringent,
since it has no purification in a ritual bath.
phrases.notes: A person can immerse and become pure, but impure meat stays impure for good.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן לֵימָא לַן דְּטוּמְאַת הַגּוּף חֲמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 by rejecting its assumption that טומאת הגוף is the stricter prohibition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: טומאת הגוף, which carries כרת, is clearly stricter, so it should take effect on top of טומאת בשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: טומאת בשר has its own severity, since it can never be purified. So neither prohibition is clearly stricter, and רבי יוסי הגלילי's view stands.
